entries.description: enable prometheus compatible metrics endpoint (default: disabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_ENDPOINT_METRICS)
entries.notes: Flag gates the Prometheus /metrics endpoint on both servers, default disabled, same env binding. GET /metrics is now always mounted and answers b10621's own 501 diagnostic when the flag is off, and the exported body opens with the llamacpp: metric families (#1440); mlxcel's additional mlxcel_ families and --metrics-port secondary listener are additive surfaces b10621 does not have.

entries.description: enable changing global properties via POST /props (default: disabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_ENDPOINT_PROPS)
entries.notes: Since #1440 the flag has b10621's exact semantics: GET /props is always mounted and --props gates POST /props, which acknowledges {"success": true} without reading the body, exactly upstream's (empty) handler. The earlier drift (flag gated GET, no POST existed) is resolved.

entries.description: number of seconds of idleness after which the server will sleep (default: -1; -1 = disabled)
entries.notes: Accepted and honored. Upstream's shape (`tools/server/server-context.cpp`): `start_loop(sleep_idle_seconds * 1000)` sleeps the task queue after the idle window, `handle_sleeping_state` calls `destroy()` (context, model, draft model, mtmd), `update_cached_responses` snapshots `/models`, `/props` and `/metrics`, and every route but those three plus `/health` calls `wait_until_no_sleep()`, so a request wakes the server and blocks until `load_model` finishes. Measured on the pinned binary with `--sleep-idle-seconds 3`: `/props.is_sleeping` flips true after the window, `/health` still answers 200, and a `/completion` afterwards takes about 0.9 s and flips it back. mlxcel sleeps the serving WORKER rather than swapping the model provider: `BatchScheduler::run`'s idle arm already blocks on the request channel, so a configured window turns that into a bounded wait whose expiry returns from the loop; the worker then drops the scheduler (which frees the weights with the `LoadedModel` it owns), takes the channel back through `into_request_rx`, clears the prompt-prefix cache (a separate `Arc` whose detached KV blocks would otherwise survive the sleep), parks on the channel, and on the next request reloads and hands that request to the rebuilt scheduler, so waking IS its prefill exactly as upstream's blocking wake is. Reaching the idle arm already means no decode batch and no queued prefill, so nothing in flight is lost. `-1` (upstream's default) and any negative value disable it; `0` arms it, upstream's own `< 0` gate. Measured on a real checkpoint with `--sleep-idle-seconds 5`: is_sleeping goes false, true after the window, and false again 0.39 s after a completion request, with `/health`, `/v1/models` and `/metrics` answering throughout. Accepted as a hidden compatibility argument, like the other b10621-only lifecycle flags.
divergence: More routes are reachable during sleep than upstream's four, and they answer without waking the server: b10621 caches `/props`, `/models` and `/metrics` because its own handlers read the destroyed `ctx_server`, while mlxcel's read `AppState` (config, tokenizer, chat template, metrics handles), none of which the sleep frees. `/tokenize`, `/detokenize`, `/apply-template` and the other prompt-inspection routes therefore answer with `is_sleeping` still true where b10621 would have woken the server to answer them (#1440).

rationale.reason: Upstream's cached-response machinery exists because `get_res_props`, `get_res_models` and its metrics render out of the server context that entering sleep destroys; the four bypass routes are the ones it could make answer without a live context. mlxcel's tokenizer, chat template, slot registry and metrics are owned by `AppState` and outlive the worker, so the same routes answer live and correctly with no snapshot, and so do the prompt-inspection routes upstream has to wake for. There is no snapshot to build and nothing to make those routes wake for: waking exists to restore the model, and none of them reads it.

entries.description: path to save slot kv cache (default: disabled)
entries.notes: Accepted on both binaries and gating POST /slots/:id_slot exactly as b10621 does (#1440). Deferred, not supported, because the persisted state is the slot's token stream plus model/tokenizer identity rather than the KV cache the flag's help text names; see the POST /slots/:id_slot entry for the recorded divergence.
divergence: The save file carries the slot's token stream and identity, not its KV cache; a restore therefore re-prefills (or adopts from the server's own prompt cache) on the next request instead of reading KV state from disk (#1440).

rationale.reason: What a save file has to survive decides what it can contain. mlxcel KV lives in MLX device arrays whose layout is chosen at startup from the cache mode, the quantization scheme and the paged block size, so a KV image would bind the file to the exact configuration that wrote it and refuse to restore under any other, while the token stream restores under all of them and rebuilds the identical KV by prefilling. The restored tokens are also what the prompt cache keys on, so a second restore of the same slot is served from cache rather than re-prefilled. The immediate 503 on a busy slot is the same kind of choice: upstream holds the client while the slot drains for an unbounded time, and answering now lets a caller decide whether to wait.
rationale.revisit_if: a KV serialization format that is portable across cache mode, quantization and paged block size exists (the #125 paged block transfer is the nearest thing in tree and is same-process), or the slot routes grow a bounded wait with an explicit deadline, at which point deferring a busy-slot action becomes expressible without an open-ended hold.

entries.description: expose slots monitoring endpoint (default: enabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_ENDPOINT_SLOTS)
entries.notes: Spelling and default (enabled) match, and LLAMA_ARG_ENDPOINT_SLOTS is honored at runtime (env_fallback_endpoint_slots, src/server/cli_input.rs) rather than as a clap env attribute, so --slots / --no-slots keep precedence over it. Since #1440 the route is always mounted and a disabled endpoint answers b10621's 501 diagnostic instead of a 404; response-field parity is tracked on the GET /slots route entry.

Mounted unconditionally with b10621's 501 diagnostic when --metrics is off, and the body exports the b10621 llamacpp: counter and gauge families name-for-name with the Process-Start-Time-Unix header and between-scrape throughput-gauge averaging (#1440). The spec_decode_* counters accumulate from the DFlash burst and MTP tick-slice drivers; the opt-in B>1 batched burst arms (MLXCEL_ENABLE_MTP_BATCH=1) and the legacy MTP_TICK_SLICE=0 burst do not feed them yet, and speculative decoding is off by default so the shipped default exports the same zeros b10621 does. The per-position spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos_total block is omitted while empty, as upstream omits it. mlxcel's additional mlxcel_ families are additive.

Since #1440 the route is mounted unconditionally like b10621 and reports the full upstream key set: default_generation_settings as {params, n_ctx}, total_slots, model identity (alias/ftype/path), modalities, media_marker, the three endpoint toggles, ui and ui_settings, chat_template and chat_template_caps (the nine jinja::caps keys), bos/eos tokens, build_info, is_sleeping and cors_proxy_enabled, plus mlxcel extension keys (kv_cache_mode, kv_bits, speculative, geometry, capabilities) that b10621 clients ignore. Since #1485 the params block also reports the grammar surfaces (grammar, grammar_lazy, grammar_triggers, preserved_tokens) so an operator can confirm what --grammar / --json-schema resolved to. The params key-set omission and the null media_marker are permanent by_design: the reported keys are exactly the settings mlxcel resolves.
divergence: default_generation_settings.params reports the resolved defaults mlxcel actually acts on under upstream's key names; b10621 task_params keys with no mlxcel analogue (min_keep, samplers, chat_format, reasoning placement, speculative.types, lora) are omitted rather than invented; the #1485 sampler surfaces (mirostat family, dynatemp, adaptive-p) are resolved and reported since they landed, the #1441 generation_settings precedent (#1440).
media_marker is null: mlxcel takes media as content parts and has no textual marker where b10621 reports mtmd's <__media__> (#1440).

default_generation_settings.params.grammar reports the GBNF the server was started with and is empty when the default came from --json-schema or --json-schema-file, because mlxcel compiles a schema through llguidance's JSON-Schema front end and has no converted grammar text to report (#1485).

rationale.reason: Reporting a task_params key mlxcel does not act on would tell an operator a setting steers generation when it steers nothing, the silent-ignore misrepresentation epic #1431 exists to remove: keys with no mlxcel analogue are omitted rather than invented (pinned by params_reports_exactly_the_documented_key_set), and media_marker is null because media arrives as content parts and no textual marker exists to report. The policy is self-correcting, as #1472 showed: n_keep and n_discard gained a real analogue there and are reported now rather than omitted.
rationale.revisit_if: mlxcel growing an analogue for an omitted key moves that key into the reported set on its own; the omission policy itself would be revisited only if a b10621 client is found to require the omitted keys to be present rather than truthful.

entries.notes: The response is b10621's slot-object shape from a real per-request slot registry: id, n_ctx, speculative, is_processing, and for a slot that has carried a task its id_task, n_prompt_tokens, n_prompt_tokens_processed, n_prompt_tokens_cache, params, and the next_token progress block, with prompt/generated redacted unless LLAMA_SERVER_SLOTS_DEBUG is set, exactly upstream's slots_debug gate. fail_on_no_slot answers the 503 no-slot envelope. The queue-admission divergence recorded here through #1499 is fixed rather than argued: the registry used to bind a slot at route entry, so a request still waiting in the scheduler queue held one away from a request the worker was serving, and with --parallel 2 and five concurrent streams one request emitted all forty-one of its frames with id_slot -1. A handle now binds on its first progress signal, so a slot is held only by a request being served; re-measured, all five requests carry a real slot on every frame. What remains is the params key subset, which follows GET /props's omitted-rather-than-invented policy.
divergence: The slot params block reports the settings mlxcel actually resolves; b10621 task_params keys with no mlxcel analogue are omitted rather than invented, the same policy GET /props records (#1440).

rationale.reason: A slot params block that echoed a b10621 key mlxcel does not act on would tell an operator the slot is honoring a setting it ignores, which is the silent-ignore misrepresentation epic #1431 exists to remove. The block is built from the same resolved options the scheduler runs, so it can only report what is real.
rationale.revisit_if: mlxcel grows an analogue for an omitted key, which moves that key into the reported set on its own; the omission policy itself would be revisited only if a b10621 client is found to require the omitted keys to be present rather than truthful.

entries.notes: Gated by --props with b10621's 501 diagnostic when off; when on it acknowledges {"success": true} without reading the body, which is exactly upstream's handler (its body is empty apart from the acknowledgement).

Save, restore and erase are served behind --slot-save-path with b10621's response schemas (n_saved/n_written, n_restored/n_read, n_erased, timings), its stoi slot-id parsing, its Invalid slot ID / Invalid action / Invalid filename refusals with fs_validate_filename ported rule for rule, atomic writes, canonical-path confinement that refuses symlink escapes, and model/tokenizer identity binding on restore (#1440).
divergence: The save file carries the slot's token stream plus model/tokenizer identity, not its KV cache; restore rehydrates tokens and the next request re-prefills (or adopts from the server's own prompt cache) instead of reading KV state from disk (#1440).
An action addressed to a slot that is processing answers 503 unavailable_error; b10621 defers the action until the slot frees and then performs it (#1440).
